openings.text: Hi, I need to book in for my medication review. Could you check what times you have free next week?
hello, the doctor wants me to get some bloods done. what slots are open thursday or friday morning?
Hi there, I got a letter saying I'm due my cervical screening. Can you look at which appointments are available?
I'm due my yearly asthma check with the nurse. Are there any free times after 4pm this week?
Hiya, need to book a pill review. What have you got available soon?
Good morning. I'd like a routine skin check of my moles. Could you see what appointments are open this month?
Can I get my flu jab booked in? Please tell me what times are free on Saturday.
Hi, the nurse said to book a follow-up for ear irrigation. Could you check the free slots for me?
I'd like a quick chat with a GP about getting a physio referral. Any openings over the next few days?
We're going abroad in the spring and I need travel jabs. Could you see when the nurse has space?
Could I book a phone appointment to go over my repeat prescriptions? Which times are free tomorrow?
got invited for an NHS Health Check. what openings do u have next week
Hello, I'm booking for my daughter's pre-school jabs. Can you check what's free in the afternoons?
I need a GP to sign a form for my life insurance. Please could you check availability?
Hi, it's time for my blood pressure check. Which days still have free appointments?
Could I get a slot to talk through my recent test results? Can you check what's open?
My letter says I'm now eligible for the shingles vaccine. Could you find me a free time?
i'm due my next b12 injection, can u check free times monday or tuesday
Need to book thyroid bloods. What's available early in the morning, before work?
I'd like to book a coil check. Could you tell me which appointments are free in the next two weeks?
I want to sign up for the stop smoking service. Can you check when an advisor is available?
I've just moved to the area and need my new patient health check. What times are free?
Is it possible to book my autumn covid booster? Please look up the free times for me.
Hi! Can I get a slot with the practice pharmacist for a routine catch-up? What's free at the moment?

items.direct: I banged my head on an open kitchen cupboard door this morning. There's a small sore lump but I feel fine otherwise.
items.indirect: had a bit of a run-in with the kitchen cupboard earlier, total clown move, just a little egg on my forehead now lol.
items.advice_request: do I need to put ice on it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: yesterday I caught my head on the edge of the car door while getting in. It hurt for a minute and there's a tender spot.
items.indirect: the car door and my skull had a disagreement yesterday, nothing dramatic, just a tender bit up top.
items.advice_request: is paracetamol okay for the soreness?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I slipped on ice outside my house two days ago and my head hit the pavement behind me. There is a bruise, but no other problems.
items.indirect: went down on the icy path on Sunday and bonked the back of my noggin. Bit bruised but I'm grand.
items.advice_request: should I get it looked at or just leave it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: my toddler headbutted me by accident last night and I now have a small bruise above my eyebrow.
items.indirect: my little one launched herself at me yesterday and our heads clashed, just a small mark on my brow, kids eh.
items.advice_request: what's best for bruising like that?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I walked into a low beam in the cellar at work on Tuesday and knocked my head. It was sore for a bit and is now only a small bump.
items.indirect: tall person problems, clipped my head on that low beam downstairs at work. Smarted a bit, nothing more really.
items.advice_request: can I keep going to the gym as normal?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I clashed heads with another player at five-a-side football on Saturday. I carried on playing and only have a bit of tenderness now.
items.indirect: took a knock in footy at the weekend, other guy came off worse probably haha. Just a bit sore where we collided.
items.advice_request: is it fine to play again this week?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I slipped off the bottom rung of a stepladder on Friday and banged my temple on the wall. Just a graze and a bump.
items.indirect: had a little wobble on the steps at the end of last week and kissed the wall with my temple, just scraped really.
items.advice_request: should I clean the graze with anything special?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I stood up too fast under the bathroom shelf and whacked my head on its corner. It bled a tiny bit but stopped straight away.
items.indirect: classic me, popped up under the shelf in the loo and caught the corner. A spot of blood but it dried up quick.
items.advice_request: will a plaster be enough?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: while cycling with my helmet on, I rode into a low tree branch. My head got knocked back but there's only a mild ache where it hit.
items.indirect: a branch got me on my ride, helmet took most of it, just a dull ache where it clonked.
items.advice_request: is a mild ache like that normal?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: the boot lid of my car came down on my head as I was loading shopping. There's a small swelling on top but I feel normal.
items.indirect: the hatchback dropped on me while I was faffing with the bags. Little swelling on the crown, nowt else.
items.advice_request: how long does swelling like this usually last?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: during a basketball game someone's elbow caught the side of my head. It stung, and there's a bruise near my ear.
items.indirect: got elbowed upside the head at hoops last nite, kinda bruised by my ear but whatever.
items.advice_request: can I take ibuprofen for the bruise?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I sat up in my bunk bed this morning and thumped my head on the ceiling. There's a sore patch but nothing else.
items.indirect: the top bunk ceiling won again this morning, scalp's a bit sore up there, that's all.
items.advice_request: is it okay to rub some arnica on it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: yesterday in kitchen I hit my head on the extractor hood when I stand up. Small bump only, I feel okay.
items.indirect: small accident with cooker hood yesterday, my head touch it hard, now little bit sore, not big problem.
items.advice_request: I need to do something for this or no?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: my dog pulled me sideways on the lead and I knocked my head against the door frame. It's a little tender to touch today.
items.indirect: the dog yanked me into the doorframe, as you do. A bit tender when I press on it but honestly fine.
items.advice_request: would a cold compress help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I bumped my head on the wall of the pool doing backstroke this week. It was sore for an hour and there's a slight lump.
items.indirect: misjudged the end of the lane, gave the wall a little tap with my head. Small lump, ego bruised more.
items.advice_request: can I still swim tomorrow?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: my forehead knocked against my son's knee on the trampoline. I've got a small bruise there.
items.indirect: bouncing with the kids went slightly wrong, caught a knee to the forehead, little bruise, survived.
items.advice_request: anything I can put on a forehead bruise?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I walked into the corner of the garage door and cut my scalp slightly. It bled for a few minutes, then stopped with pressure.
items.indirect: the garage door got me, small nick on my scalp. Bled like scalps do but stopped once I held a towel on it.
items.advice_request: does a small scalp cut need stitches?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I tripped on the rug at home on Monday and caught my forehead on the coffee table. I got straight up and only have a bruise.
items.indirect: had a silly trip in the hallway and my forehead met the furniture. Purple now, but I was up again in a jiffy.
items.advice_request: is there a cream that helps bruises fade?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: I took a knock to the head in a rugby tackle on Saturday. I was checked pitchside, felt fine, and it's only a bit sore now.
items.indirect: got clattered in a tackle at rugby, physio gave me the once-over, all good, just tender.
items.advice_request: how soon can I go back to training?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: the bus braked hard and my head bumped sideways into the window. It's slightly sore but I've had no other effects.
items.indirect: driver slammed the anchors on and my head went thunk on the glass. Bit embarrassing, slight soreness, that's it.
items.advice_request: do I need to rest or can I work as normal?
items.source_ref: NICE NG232 Head injury (2023): CT within 8 hours for adults on anticoagulants after head injury

items.direct: a few times this week I've gone shaky and sweaty late in the morning, and it settles once I've eaten something.
items.indirect: keep getting a bit wobbly and clammy before lunch. A biscuit sorts me out so it's probably just me being greedy.
items.advice_request: should I just carry snacks around?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I've been waking at night drenched in sweat with my heart racing, and I feel better after a glass of juice.
items.indirect: had some sweaty nights lately, wake up all damp with my ticker going like the clappers. Bit of juice and I'm off back to sleep.
items.advice_request: could it just be the room being too warm?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: on Wednesday afternoon I got confused at my desk and couldn't follow an email, and I was sweaty. Eating a sandwich fixed it.
items.indirect: had a weird foggy moment at work midweek, words just weren't going in. Bit sweaty, then a sarnie and I was back to normal.
items.advice_request: is that just stress, do you think?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: my partner says I get very irritable, shaky and pale when I go too long without food, and it's happening more often.
items.indirect: apparently I'm a nightmare when I'm hangry these days. Go pale and trembly, and the other half's noticed it a lot more.
items.advice_request: is there a diet that helps with this?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: my vision goes blurry and I feel trembly if I skip a meal, but it clears within a few minutes of eating.
items.indirect: eyes go a bit funny and I get the shakes if I miss brekkie. Sorts itself once I've had a bite.
items.advice_request: do I need an eye test as well?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: yesterday in the supermarket I nearly fainted, went cold and sweaty, and had to sit down and eat chocolate before I felt okay.
items.indirect: almost keeled over in the shop yesterday, came over all cold and clammy. A Mars bar by the tills saved me haha.
items.advice_request: would drinking more water help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I keep getting a fluttery heartbeat along with strong hunger in the afternoons, and it goes after a snack.
items.indirect: tbh my heart does this flutter thing around 3pm and I'm suddenly starving. Snack fixes it, prob just my body being dramatic.
items.advice_request: could cutting out coffee help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: after my morning runs I've been getting shaky, sweaty and lightheaded, much more than I used to, until I eat.
items.indirect: post-run I'm a trembly mess lately, way worse than normal. Have to grab a banana before I can function.
items.advice_request: should I eat before I run?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I've been getting super shaky and my hands sweat loads in class before lunch, and my friend gave me sweets which helped.
items.indirect: ngl I go all jittery and sweaty in third period, my mate gives me haribo and then I'm fine.
items.advice_request: is it bad to just eat sweets for it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I've been having bad dreams, waking up sweaty, and getting a headache in the mornings that eases once I have breakfast.
items.indirect: nights have been rubbish, vivid dreams, damp sheets, and a groggy thick head when I wake up till I've had my toast.
items.advice_request: could that be a sleep problem?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: sometimes my hands are shaking and I am sweating very much before dinner, then I eat and it go away.
items.indirect: before dinner time I feel not good, little shaking, much sweat, after food is okay, maybe I am only tired.
items.advice_request: is this normal or I need test?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I've noticed my lips tingle and I feel jittery when I'm late eating, and it eases off after I've had something.
items.indirect: funny pins and needles round my mouth and the jitters if lunch is late. Goes away with grub.
items.advice_request: is that a vitamin thing?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: last week while driving I suddenly felt shaky, sweaty and couldn't concentrate, so I pulled over and ate, and it passed.
items.indirect: had a wobbly spell at the wheel the other day, sweaty and couldn't think straight. Pulled in for a snack and I was right as rain.
items.advice_request: is it safe for me to keep driving?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I get sudden waves of feeling anxious, sweaty and trembling, usually a few hours after a meal, and food calms it.
items.indirect: out of the blue I get this panicky quivery feeling a few hours after eating. A snack takes the edge off, probably just nerves.
items.advice_request: do you think it's anxiety?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: twice this month I've woken up confused and soaked in sweat, and my husband had to give me a sugary drink before I made sense.
items.indirect: himself says I was talking nonsense when I woke a couple of times recently, all sweaty. He gave me some Lucozade and I came round.
items.advice_request: should I see a sleep clinic?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: my legs go weak and my heart pounds if I go a few hours without food, and I feel a lot better after eating.
items.indirect: jelly legs and a thumping heart if I go too long between meals, a quick bite and I perk right up.
items.advice_request: would eating little and often help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: the morning after a few drinks I wake up shaking, sweating and feeling faint, more than a normal hangover, until I eat.
items.indirect: hangovers have gone weird. I wake up trembling and drippy and nearly passing out, not just the usual sore head. Food helps.
items.advice_request: should I just drink less?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: my kids noticed I went pale, quiet and couldn't answer them properly at teatime, and I was sweaty; I was fine after eating.
items.indirect: kids said I went a bit vacant and grey before tea, couldn't string a sentence, bit clammy. Back to myself once I'd had food.
items.advice_request: is that just tiredness from work?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: I've been feeling really lightheaded and shaky in the late afternoon, and my coworkers say I look gray until I get a snack.
items.indirect: around 4 I get kinda woozy and trembly and my coworkers joke I look like a ghost til I grab some chips.
items.advice_request: would a protein bar help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: during long meetings I start sweating, trembling and my heart races, and it only stops once I eat something sweet.
items.indirect: long meetings do me in. I get sweaty and quivery with a racing pulse, only a sugary something calms it down.
items.advice_request: do I need any tests?
items.source_ref: NICE NG28 / NG17: recognising hypoglycaemia in people on insulin or sulfonylureas

items.direct: there's a small sore on my heel that hasn't healed after three weeks, even though I've kept it covered.
items.indirect: got a little spot on my heel that's taking its sweet time to heal, few weeks now, it's only small though.
items.advice_request: should I try a different dressing?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: I got a blister on my big toe on a walk ten days ago and it has burst and still looks raw.
items.indirect: my big toe got a hiking blister that popped ages ago and it's still kinda raw-looking, not a big deal.
items.advice_request: can I use a blister plaster on it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: the skin on my heels has cracked deeply and one of the cracks bled a little this week.
items.indirect: my heels are like the Sahara, and one of the splits had a little bleed this week.
items.advice_request: is there a good cream for cracked heels?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: two of the toes on my right foot have looked bluish and felt cold for about a week.
items.indirect: a couple of my right toes have gone a funny purply shade and they're always chilly lately.
items.advice_request: would thicker socks help?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: my left foot has become swollen and warm across the middle, though I can't remember hurting it.
items.indirect: left foot's puffed up and feels hot in the middle for no reason, didn't twist it or anything, weird.
items.advice_request: should I rest it and put it up?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: my big toenail is ingrown and the skin beside it is red and sore.
items.indirect: toenail's digging into the side of my toe again and it's all pink and angry looking.
items.advice_request: can I soak it in salt water?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: the hard skin under the ball of my foot bled when I took my sock off last night.
items.indirect: found a bit of blood on my sock from that tough patch under my foot, it's just the callus I reckon.
items.advice_request: is it okay to file it down myself?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: I stood on a piece of glass a week ago and the cut on my sole doesn't seem to be closing up.
items.indirect: trod on some glass last week, the nick on the bottom of my foot is still sort of open, it's tiny honestly.
items.advice_request: do I need a tetanus jab?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: I found a sore on my foot from a stone in my shoe that I hadn't even felt.
items.indirect: funny thing, walked about all day with a pebble in my trainer and didn't notice, left a little sore patch.
items.advice_request: should I keep it dry or let it breathe?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: there's a split between my fourth and fifth toes that has been weeping for a week.
items.indirect: a little crack between my last two toes keeps going soggy and won't dry up.
items.advice_request: would talc help dry it out?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: new shoes rubbed the side of my little toe and the skin broke, and it's still red after five days.
items.indirect: my new work shoes took the skin off my pinky toe, still a bit red nearly a week on.
items.advice_request: should I stop wearing those shoes?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: on my foot there is small wound under the toe, it is there one month and not closing.
items.indirect: under my toe is little open place, maybe one month already, I put cream, not much change.
items.advice_request: which cream is better for this?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: I stubbed my second toe last week and it's still swollen and red, more than I expected.
items.indirect: stubbed my toe on the bed leg the other week, still puffy and pinkish, slow healer I guess.
items.advice_request: could it be broken?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: my shoe has been rubbing the bone on the side of my ankle and it's left a small open patch.
items.indirect: ankle bone's got a little raw bit where my boots dig in, nothing major.
items.advice_request: is a padded sock worth trying?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems: active diabetic foot problem needs referral to the foot protection service or MDT

items.direct: the redness around a cut on my foot is spreading up towards my ankle, and I've had a fever and chills since yesterday.
items.indirect: that scratch on my foot's gone pink and the pink seems to be creeping up past my ankle. Been shivery and hot since yesterday too, prob a bug.
items.advice_request: should I draw round the red bit and watch it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: the tip of one of my toes has turned black and hard over the past few days.
items.indirect: end of my toe has gone a dark colour, kinda black and crusty. It doesn't really hurt so maybe it's just bruised?
items.advice_request: can I wait and see if it goes back to normal?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: there's a deep hole on the sole of my foot that is oozing yellow-green pus and smells bad.
items.indirect: the sore underneath my foot has gone a bit gunky, yellowish stuff coming out and a whiffy smell. I've been sticking plasters on.
items.advice_request: would antiseptic cream clear it up?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: my foot is red, hot and very swollen around an ulcer, and there are red lines running up my leg.
items.indirect: my foot's angry and puffy round that sore and there are some reddish streaky lines heading up my shin, might just be sock marks.
items.advice_request: is it alright to keep walking on it?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: a blister on my heel has turned dark and the skin around it looks red and feels hot, and I feel feverish and unwell.
items.indirect: the blister on my heel's gone a dodgy dark colour, skin round it is hot, and I'm feeling a bit rough and fluey with it.
items.advice_request: should I pop it to let it drain?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: I can see something white deep in the wound on my toe and it keeps leaking fluid.
items.indirect: the cut on my toe goes quite deep and there's a whitish bit at the bottom, keeps leaking. Prob just how it heals?
items.advice_request: how often should I change the dressing?
items.source_ref: NICE NG19 Diabetic foot problems rec 1.3.4: refer immediately (limb-threatening ischaemia, gangrene, ulcer with fever or sepsis, deep infection)

items.direct: I've had a crushing pain in the centre of my chest for the last half hour, spreading into my left arm, and I'm sweating.
items.indirect: there's a heavy squeezing feeling across my ribs that's been going on about thirty minutes, kind of runs down my arm and I'm clammy, probably indigestion?
items.advice_request: should I take an antacid and lie down?
items.source_ref: NICE CG95 Chest pain of recent onset rec 1.1 (suspected ACS: emergency referral)

items.direct: my dad has had chest pain going up into his jaw for about twenty minutes and he looks grey and sweaty.
items.indirect: my dad's sat in his chair rubbing his breastbone, says it's like a band, his jaw aches and he's gone a bit grey. He says it's just wind.
items.advice_request: would some peppermint tea settle him?
items.source_ref: NICE CG95 Chest pain of recent onset rec 1.1 (suspected ACS: emergency referral)

items.direct: I get tight chest pain and breathlessness on stairs, and today it started while I was sitting still and it hasn't gone away.
items.indirect: that tightness I used to get climbing up to bed turned up while I was just watching telly, and it's still hanging about. Short of puff too.
items.advice_request: can I just wait for it to ease off?
items.source_ref: NICE CG95 Chest pain of recent onset rec 1.1 (suspected ACS: emergency referral)

items.direct: I've had a pressure in my chest with nausea and pain between my shoulder blades that started an hour ago.
items.indirect: feels like an elephant's sat on me, bit sick, and an ache between my shoulder blades since about an hour ago. Probably slept funny.
items.advice_request: is a hot water bottle on my back a good idea?
items.source_ref: NICE CG95 Chest pain of recent onset rec 1.1 (suspected ACS: emergency referral)

items.direct: my face dropped on one side and my right arm went weak for about ten minutes this morning, then it went back to normal.
items.indirect: had a strange little episode this morning where my smile went lopsided and my arm felt dead heavy for a few minutes. All fine now though.
items.advice_request: since it's passed, can it wait for a normal appointment?
items.source_ref: NICE NG128 Stroke and TIA rec 1.1 (FAST, immediate referral)

items.direct: my mum's speech suddenly became slurred about twenty minutes ago and she can't lift her left arm properly.
items.indirect: mum's been talking a bit funny since a little while ago, words coming out mushy, and she's not really using her left hand. She says she's just tired.
